{{Short description|American chemist}}

'''Frank B. Mallory''' (March 17, 1933 - November 7, 2017)<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.mcconaghyfuneralhome.com/obituary/frank-mallory|title=Frank B. Mallory of Bryn Mawr, Pennsylvania }}</ref><ref name="DepartmentObit">{{cite web |url= https://www.brynmawr.edu/chemistry/memoriam-dr-frank-mallory |title= In Memoriam: Dr. Frank Mallory |publisher= [[Bryn Mawr College]] Department of Chemistry }}</ref> was a professor of [[organic chemistry]] at [[Bryn Mawr College]]. He was on faculty at Bryn Mawr for 54 years, the longest-serving faculty member in the school's history.<ref name="DepartmentObit"/> His work focused on [[photochemistry]], [[NMR spectroscopy]], and [[solid-state chemistry]]. The [[Mallory reaction]] is an [[organic name reaction]] he discovered while a graduate student. Mallory's professional honors include a [[John Simon Guggenheim Memorial Foundation]] fellowship and a [[Sloan Research Fellowship]].<ref name="CassidyObit">{{cite web |url= https://www.brynmawr.edu/news/remembering-distinguished-career-long-time-professor-chemistry-frank-mallory |title= Remembering the Distinguished Career of Long-Time Professor of Chemistry Frank Mallory |first= Kim |last= Cassidy |author-link= Kimberly Wright Cassidy |date= November 16, 2017 }}</ref>
